questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go abroad, but not too far, so I still had the opportunity to go back home some weekends and have visits from my family. I also really wanted to go to a German speaking country, since I am learning German. And Berlin is a really cool and big city that I wanted to get to know.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received a lot of assistance from the central erasmus office at FU as well as the erasmus office at the Otto Suhr Institute for Political Science in terms of emails.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was lucky to get a dorm room that was reserved for exchange students at FU. My impression is that it is extremely difficult to find an affordable place to live in Berlin.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is cool:) I don't think there is an opportunity to live on campus at FU Berlin. But as a student you have unlimited public transportation.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I don't really remember now

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I don't remember

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was successful in registrering for classes in the Political Science MA, but not for classes from the other MA's at the same institute.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't know

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: All MA courses, some were research oriented.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A lot more interactive! At FU I did seminars, whereas I have mostly done lectures at UCPH. Also, at FU there was a requirement of active participation (through presentations and weekly reading notes/discussion points), and at UCPH you don't even have to show up.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Researching the EU,
Peace Building in South Asia from IR Perspectives,
The Semantics, Metaphysics and Politics of Race,
Radical politics and (non)violent resistance,
Democratic Backsliding? The United States in Perspective

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of them! They were very interesting.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Buying inventory for my dorm room (which was supposedly furnitured, but did not have any kitchen supplies e.g.).
Tickets home when I was sick for a few weeks in a row.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is generally cheaper than in Copenhagen. The same goes for museums.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The erasmus club at FU Berlin offered some events, e.g. going to the opera, city tours. However, I did not participate in any of them as they did not fit my schedule.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did not partake in any.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Going to the Botanical Garden! And sightseeing, going for walks in Berlin's different neighborhoods.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I don't know. Be open and friendly? Try to talk some German if possible maybe?

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People at Uni were a lot kinder than I have experienced in Copenhagen. E.g. saying hello and 'Tchau' . And going to the cafeteria together.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Know that there is a lot of paperwork required (I think this goes for any exchange semester)
Know that the course selection is limited if you only want to take English courses
And be aware that the semester structure is different

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can either do a Teilnahme- or Leistungscchein for each course (3 or 7 ECTS credits).

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I gained a lot more professional confidence through giving presentations and discussing with my peers in class (seminar style).

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being alone and very stressed with school.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
